_about: Groups of kanji that are easy to mistake for one another. Used to pick multiple-choice distractors that are actually hard: 待 against 持 rather than against whatever happened to sit nearby in the frequency list.
_why: Distractors drawn from frequency neighbours are plausible but not difficult — nothing about 待 vs 会 tests whether you can read 待. Confusion between similar-looking characters is the dominant failure mode in real reading, and it was the one thing the app never asked about.
_format: groups is a list of strings; every kanji in a string is considered confusable with every other in it. A kanji may appear in more than one group. Groups mix two kinds of similarity: near-identical whole shapes (土/士, 未/末) and a shared element that dominates the character (待/持/特, 晴/清/静).
_scope: Curated, not computed: the dataset carries no radical or component decomposition, and stroke count alone is a poor proxy — 一 and 乙 share a count and look nothing alike. Weighted toward the frequent range, where a learner meets these first. Add your own in userdata/similar.local.json, same shape.
